items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: And Jimmy Mundy was writing the arrangements.

ctx.x: I was getting like two, three record dates a day, three and four record dates, man, because during this time, there were a lot of big bands, you know, like integrated bands, cats was calling me when they knew I was out -- you know, like out in Romeo and those cats in Hymie Schertzef and all them cats, they were giving me rings and all that kind of stuff. So we were doing a lot of things for singers. They still had a lot of singers in those days, big bands and things.

And man, I didn't know. I said, "Man, I didn't know it was like this and I don't have to go out of town?" So when they asked me to go -- they asked me to come back to the band. I says, "Uh-uh." Because I had found what I really wanted to -- I could play much more, you know what I mean? And I was meeting cats and I was staying at home with my family. So that's why I didn't go out. So then I worked with Lips, Hot Lips, for a while. He had some theater dates and things and I did some things with him and then who…
